If you make players have perfect information of the opposing deck, you probably remove more skillcap rather than increase it? Why? Playing with limited information or no information requires skill of: 1. Anticipating what archetype you play against.  2. How do you want to mulligan 3. What line is your opponent likely to go 4. What your opponent has in your hand aka what cards do I play around 5. Knowing how to play to your own outs 6. Evaluating the amount of tempo and card advantage If you work with perfect information you neglect most of the mentioned above and it creates possibly like 1-2 lines of play to go with. Not to mention 90% of the games would be slow/boring as fuck control matchups (and by slow/boring as fuck I mean if there is a guy who normally enjoys playing control, he would be disgusted by that) that would surely end up in fatigue wars. The deck would contain answers and threats only and nobody would be able to push through your threat for more than 1 turn at maximum.  TL;DR. Removing RNG removes much of the skill cap, since playing around randomness and neglecting its influence is the true challenge here.
